radiology_report:
Subject: Multiparametric MRI Prostate | Facility: Catharina Ziekenhuis, Eindhoven | Date: 28 February 2025

Assessment prompted by a 2.7 ng/mL PSA measurement and a previous PI-RADS 2 designation.

Glandular dimensions register at 56.0 mL on volumetric analysis. T2 sequences reveal a uniformly textured organ with subtle central zone hypertrophy. An 8 mm hypointense focus occupies the right mid-gland peripheral zone, yet lacks diffusion restriction and demonstrates delayed enhancement kinetics, favoring a benign etiology such as a retention cyst or nodular hyperplasia. No focal abnormalities warrant concern. The seminal vesicles and neurovascular bundles maintain normal architecture. Pelvic imaging shows no extraprostatic spread or nodal enlargement.

PI-RADS 2. Prostate volume 56.0 mL, PSA density 0.05 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.48990974.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: A PSA reading of 2.9 ng/mL was recorded in June 2024, representing an increase from the 1.4 ng/mL baseline documented in October 2023. Motivated by the rising trajectory and the patient’s apprehension about invasive diagnostics, a referral to urology was initiated for targeted PSA assessment and multiparametric MRI scheduling. Antibacterial therapy was withheld due to absent infectious markers, while urinary complaints continue to be observed without pharmacological intervention.
